svg.title: Read each template and each new strand separately
svg.desc: Two rust parental backbones open to the left of a fork moving right. The upper template runs3′ left to5′ right and supports teal leading DNA growing5′ left to3′ right toward the fork. The lower template runs5′ left to3′ right; three short new fragments each have a purple5′ primer at their right end and a3′ growing end toward the left, away from the advancing fork. Every new strand therefore grows5′→3′ while its template is read3′→5′. A leading primer and detailed enzyme structures are omitted explicitly. Helicase separates paired strands rather than shredding backbones; polymerase extends an existing3′ end; primer processing/replacement precedes ligase sealing of suitable nicks. This diagram does not portray the daughter strands as chemically growing backward or ligase filling long sequence gaps.

g.text: Read each template and each new strand separately
A right-moving fork explains why one daughter strand is assembled in fragments.
Leading: continuous synthesis toward the fork
Lagging: each fragment grows 5′→3′ away from the advancing fork.
Purple = short primer at the 5′ end of each illustrated fragment; a leading primer is omitted.
Helicase separates paired strands. Polymerase extends an available 3′ end, reading template 3′→5′.
Primers are processed/replaced; ligase seals suitable backbone nicks after adjacent DNA is present.
Geometry is schematic: lagging synthesis is discontinuous, never chemically 3′→5′.
